title: Lego Robotics for Elementary Students
location: RecRoom, 1 Lackawanna Plaza, Ste. 6, Montclair, 07042, United States
description:
LEGO Robotics for Elementary Kids (Grades K–5) 
LEGO Robotics at Kinetic Minds introduces kids to engineering and beginner coding through hands-on building, testing, and problem-solving using LEGO robotics kits. 
In this small-group, drop-in friendly workshop, kids work in pairs to build real robots, program simple behaviors, and improve their designs through guided challenges. The focus is on curiosity, experimentation, and learning how things work—there’s no single “right” build and no step-by-step cookie-cutter instructions. 
Workshops are intentionally capped at a low student-to-instructor ratio to support collaboration, confidence, and meaningful learning. 
Kids will explore:
• Engineering and building with LEGO robotics components
• Beginner coding concepts (motors, sensors, cause and effect)
• Testing, debugging, and iterating designs
• Teamwork, communication, and explaining ideas 
Details:
• 60-minute session
• Small-group format
• No prior experience required 
Community Sponsorship:
20% of seats are reserved for community sponsorship. Families interested in sponsored spots can email info@kineticmindscreative.com
for details.

title: Casual Volleyball - North Jersey
description:
North Jersey Bowling, Volleyball, Tennis And More
We're a group of people who will start by hitting the ball around for the first 20-30 minutes and then will break up into 2-4 teams for two or three hours of play.

If we have more than 20 people show up, we'll break up into three or four teams of 6 (Some may have 7, 8 or 9. Additional players just rotate into play). Games will be to 10 points. Rally scoring. Winner stays on (unless a team has won four straight).

We'll be heading outdoors to the hard court in Leonia off Overpeck County Pk Driveway in the Overpeck County Park.

\*\*\* After playing, we'll be likely heading to Tropical Juice Bar, an idea of regular attendee Kate, for a drink and snack. It's located at 60 River St. in Hackensack. Feel free to join us or suggest another spot for a post-volleyball hangout. \*\*\*

There's no fee to play volleyball and nothing else you need to do besides show up. Come anytime!! All are welcome!!! We're not in a league and are not here to analyze your form. We're more for people who haven't played in months, maybe years, and just want to occasionally play again and hang out.

Directions: You can Google "Volleyball Court in Leonia" and it should come up. Or type 41 Willow Tree Road, Leonia, NJ 07605 into your GPS, but note that it's not on Willow Tree Road, just near it. Instead, turn onto Overpeck County Pk Driveway off Fort Lee Road (Degraw Avenue). It is past the tennis courts and near a basketball court and track. You can try Googling Leonia High School as well. That should help you find it.

We don't have the court reserved and if it happens to be taken, we may play with those already occupying it or we will try to relocate on the fly. It's certainly possible that we may have to cancel that day if we can't find a suitable spot. Please keep that in mind. And if it's looking like it'll rain or snow, I'll make a call on whether to cancel around an hour ahead of time.

Please bring a ball and net if you have them for possible use during the game. Feel free to bring a speaker for music, or snacks and drinks for consumption during play.

If you have trouble finding the court or group, you can call or text Andy Milone at 201-234-9609. There is plenty of parking and an open bathroom at the park.

Hope you'll join us for our 19th "official" volleyball event. Questions or comments? You can message Andy on Meetup, or call/text him at 201-234-9609. Check out bowling, soccer, volleyball, tennis or one of our other activities at: www.meetup.com/north-jersey-bowling-soccer-volleyball

If interested in staying touch with group members or conversing about future events, feel free to inquire about our WhatsApp group chat.

title: Crock of Pequannock Hike
description:
Metrotrails: NJ, PA, NY Metropolitan Area Hiking and More!
Join us for this next hike in our Passaic Watershed series, this time continuing up the Pequannock and Ramapo Rivers from where we last left off in Pompton Plains!
We'll meet at 9 am at Plaza 23, which has the Stop and Shop and Buy Rite Liquors closer to Jackson Avenue.
This is a 15 mile loop, so we'll begin right there, and make our way along Jackson to the former Morris Canal crossing. If anyone wants to go and see the old Pompton Lock, many can do this and hike through while I'll head with the stroller on parallel roads out and around Riverview Farm.
We will follow several pleasant back roads and streets to the north, visit the historic Schuyler-Colfax House, and see the Pompton Lake Dam.
From there we will had south on more of the Morris Canal Greenway, which was where it followed the slackwater of the river.
We'll pass through Mathes Avenue Woodlands, and several other properties to Ventimiglia tracts, then to Willow Field.
We get back on street a short bit, then back to Hershfield Park where we'll do a little loop.
We'll make our way toward Pompton Junction before turning back tracing the former Greenwood Lake Branch of the Erie Railroad again.
Most of this is active, so we'll be on closely parallel stuff on this part.
Toward the end, it becomes the rail trail again which we'll follow to where we left off, then back to the plaza to close the loop.
If needed, contact me at 908 343 8374

title: Let's Walk!! Rahway River Park
description:
Let's Walk!!
**This walk begins at 8:30 AM**
Please plan to arrive 5 minutes early. The walk will start promptly.

Come get some steps before heading off to a Memorial Day picnic or BBQ. We'll do the perimeter loop and the lake loop, together they are about 2 miles.
The group will do 2 circuits (4 miles) in 90 minutes, but all are welcome to stop after one or stay longer. The path is 100% paved.
**Wear comfortable shoes and don't forget your water.**

[Perimeter Loop](https://www.alltrails.com/trail/us/new-jersey/rahway-river-perimeter-loop?u=i&sh=vgtzxk)
[Lake Loop](https://www.alltrails.com/trail/us/new-jersey/lake-rahway-loop?u=i&sh=vgtzxk)

Meet near the Ulrich pool house. There are parking lots on both sides of Parkway Drive and street parking nearby.

Disclaimer: If you join us for a hike, please understand that you are responsible for your own preparedness and well-being and will hold no one else liable in case of injury or mishap.

This class welcomes all levels from beginner to experienced yogis. Bring your own yoga mat and props.

title: CEDAR GROVE PARK WALK
description:
Let's Walk!!
**This walk begins at 6:00 PM**

You can **park** in the **Robert J. O'Toole Community Center** parking lot located at **199 Fairview Ave, Cedar Grove, NJ 07009**

**Meet us under the gazebos** at the park directly across the street.

We will be walking the paved walking path that meanders over foot bridges and past little “workout stations.”

We will walk about 3 - 4 miles. There are options to break off from the walk if you need to.

Bathrooms are available.

Cedar Grove Park is the newest addition to the Essex County Park System, formally dedicated on December 12, 2016. At 77 acres, it is the fourth largest park in the county parks system. The park features the Robert J. O'Toole Community Center, four bocce courts, a farm themed playground area and three fitness stations along meandering walking paths.

Rain or extreme weather will cancel the event.

PLEASE ARRIVE 5 MINUTES PRIOR TO START TIME.

Disclaimer: If you join us for a hike, please understand that you are responsible for your own preparedness and well-being and will hold no one else liable in case of injury or mishap.

description:
North Jersey Bowling, Volleyball, Tennis And More
Meet & Greet for Christian Singles, ages 25-45. This is an online event.

I asked Chat GPT some good questions to ask and we will be taking turns answering them. We will go through as many questions as we can in the limited time.

Chat GPT says:

### 🌿 Faith & Relationship with Values

* What role does your faith play in your daily life?
* What does a Christ-centered relationship mean to you?
* What qualities are most important to you in a partner?
* How do you usually grow spiritually?
* What’s something God has been teaching you recently?
* What kind of relationship do you hope to have one day?
* What are your biggest relationship values?
* What does healthy communication look like to you?
* What kind of family environment do you hope to build someday?
* What does commitment mean to you?

### 💛 Getting to Know Each Other

* What’s your favorite way to spend your weekends?
* What’s something people are usually surprised to learn about you?
* What’s a hobby or interest you wish you had more time for?
* What kind of personality are you naturally drawn to?
* Are you more introverted or extroverted?
* What’s your favorite worship song or Christian artist right now?
* What’s one thing that always makes you feel encouraged?
* What’s your favorite Bible verse and why?
* What kind of conversations do you enjoy most?
* What’s something you’re passionate about?

### 🤍 Deeper Dating Questions

* How do you handle conflict or disagreements?
* What boundaries are important to you while dating?
* What does spiritual leadership look like to you?
* How important is church involvement to you?
* What are you praying for in your future relationship?
* How do you balance grace and accountability?
* What kind of support helps you feel cared for?
* What are some lessons you’ve learned from past relationships?
* How do you stay grounded during difficult seasons?
* What are your long-term goals and hopes?

### 💍 Bible Study Questions

* What’s one prayer God has answered in your life?
* What Bible story inspires you most?
* What’s something you appreciate in Christian friendships?
* What does “loving like Jesus” look like in relationships?
* What’s one quality you admire in strong Christian couples?
* What’s something young Christians struggle with in dating today?
* How can relationships help people grow spiritually?
* What’s one piece of dating advice you think is underrated?
* What’s your favorite way to serve others?
* What helps you stay encouraged in your faith?

### 🌸 Fun Questions

* Beach or mountains?
* Worship night or game night?
* Sunrise or sunset?
* Texting or FaceTime?
* Sweet snacks or salty snacks?
* Road trip or staycation?
* Big group hangout or one-on-one time?
* Fancy dinner or casual café?
* Books or podcasts?

### 📖 Fun but Meaningful

* Which person in the Bible do you relate to most and why?
* If you could ask God one question right now, what would it be?
* What does your “dream life” look like if God is at the center?

title: Rock Voices Montclair: Three Open-House Opportunities - come sing with our Community Rock Choir!
location: 153 Park St, Montclair, NJ 07042, 153 Park St., Montclair, 07042, United States
description:
If you’ve been missing how much fun it is to sing with other people – or always wanted to try it out for the first time – come check out Rock Voices Montclair as we get our Summer 2026 “MUSIC FROM THE MOVIES” Season started! 
We are a fun and friendly community choir for adults – with an emphasis on community – and we sing only ROCK, pop, and other contemporary music. There are never any auditions required to join, and ALL ARE WELCOME. Rock Voices has 35+ chapters across the Northeast US and Portland, and we’ve been making music in Montclair since the Fall of 2023. 
We rehearse on Tuesday nights from 7-9pm in Montclair, with our next season starting on May 19th, and a Summer Concert in August. Enrollment for the season is open through June 8th. (We also record all of our rehearsals, so if you’ve already got some warm-weather vacay plans in the mix, no worries at all – we’ve got you covered with as many replays as needed!) 
This season’s Open House Rehearsal dates are 5/19, 5/26, and 6/2 – please join us at one, two, or all three, as we start our 12-week session. There’s no obligation with these Open Houses, so just come hang out with us – have some snacks, make some new friends, sing some songs you probably know…and see what you think! 
You can check out our full set list for the season at www.RockVoices.com – and you can sign up there too, just so we know to look out for you, and to have enough sheet music (and snacks!) ready. Plus it’ll be faster than waiting in line to do it when you get there. 
Here’s our direct link: https://rockvoices.com/choir_location/montclair-nj/ 
Please follow us on FB, IG, and YouTube @RockVoicesMontclairNJ to learn more about us, and to find our FB event page and Enrollment FAQs too – we hope to sing with you soon!

title: Weekly Labyrinth Walks, Wednesdays 11am-1pm
description: Weekly: Wednesdays 11am-1pm in the Sanctuary  Take your soul for a walk on the labyrinth.  We are pleased to offer labyrinth walks each Wednesday in the mid-day as a chance to connect with your soul in our beautiful sanctuary. The labyrinth is an ancient spiritual tool , a mode of “walking prayer” that invites us to go deeper in our walk with God.  Our labyrinth, modeled on one in Chartes Cathedral in France, sits as the center of our Sanctuary, a constant metaphor for our spiritual lives.  Just like the labyrinth, our lives are not linear, but filled with twists and turns.  Sometimes we make great progress, and other times we feel we are going backwards.  But if we trust in the path we will find ourselves in the center -- the heart of God. All are welcome to take their souls out for a healing walk... no experience necessary!  Check out this lovely write up on Baristanet from the Spring 2014. Watch this video to find out more about walking the labyrinth. If you’ve never done so come out one Wednesday evening and give it a try. It is a wonderful way to nourish your soul and spend some quiet time in prayer or meditation.

title: (CXLD) Wine Confidence 101: Understanding the Basics
location: Montclair Public Library
description:
This is a paid Adult School class. Click here to register.

This introductory course offers a comprehensive overview of essential wine concepts, designed to establish or strengthen your foundational knowledge and support your ongoing appreciation of wine. 

Over the 5-week course, we will review the primary grape varieties and styles of dry white, rosé, red, and sparkling wines, as well as explore viticulture fundamentals and the winemaking process. We will explore the major wine-producing countries and differences among grape varieties and wine styles. We will review how to taste and critically evaluate wine from visual assessment through aftertaste. For historical context, the course provides an overview of wine’s origins, its evolution, and the business aspects of winemaking. A solid foundation also includes guidance on appropriate tools for opening wine bottles, optimal storage, and serving temperatures to enhance your overall wine experience. 

By the end of the 5-week class, you will have gained a deeper understanding of the many aspects of dry and sparkling wines so you are thoroughly conversant about wine and have tasted between 20 – 25 different wines from around the world!

title: Home Repair Essentials NEW
location: Montclair - Montclair High School, Montclair Public Library
description:
This is a paid Adult School class. Click here to register. 

Learn the fundamentals of home repair in this practical, hands-on workshop taught by Robert Haas, instructor of the popular Woodworking 101 and Advanced Woodworking classes. Held at Montclair High School, this course gives participants a behind-the-walls look at how common home features are built and maintained.

During the class, Robert will construct two demonstration walls that include doors and a window, showing how these elements are installed and how typical wall structures are assembled. Participants will also learn how traditional double-hung windows operate and how they can be repaired, including basic glass pane replacement.

The workshop will also introduce the basics of residential wiring, demonstrating how outlets and lighting are installed and connected. Throughout the session, Robert will answer questions and offer guidance on a wide range of home repair topics.

Whether you're a homeowner looking to handle basic repairs yourself or simply curious about how things in your home work, this class provides practical knowledge you can use right away.

title: Centralized Data Lakes in the Cloud: Scalable and Governed Architectures
description:
Cloud Data Driven
Global data creation is projected to reach 175 zettabytes, with enterprises managing the majority of this growth. In data-intensive industries, organizations process an average of 9.1 petabytes per enterprise, exposing the limitations of traditional data warehouses. Yet 76% of organizations struggle with data lake governance, and 68% lack clear data ownership.

This session presents a research-backed framework for building centralized, cloud-based data lakes that deliver measurable improvements in performance, cost, and governance. Mature implementations achieve 3.2× faster time-to-insight, 54% reduction in data preparation effort, and 59.3% lower storage costs. Multi-layered architectures improve query performance by 73%, increase resource utilization by 81%, and reduce bottlenecks by 67.4%.

Cloud-native distributed storage supports 3.2× higher performance for mixed workloads, enables 8.7× more concurrent users, and delivers 99.99% availability. Beyond architecture, strong governance and master data management reduce inconsistencies by 83.6%, increase data utilization by 412%, and improve decision-making speed by 47.2%.

Security-by-design approaches reduce unauthorized access by 78.4%, lower breach likelihood by 56.2%, and decrease compliance penalties by 85.4%.

Attendees will gain practical, data-driven strategies to design scalable, secure, and governance-centric cloud data lakes.

title: Inspiration trap creativity workshop
description:

6,7&8pm Issyra Gallery presents - Inspiration Trap Creativity workshop

Only 10 attendees allowed social distancing and mandatory mask wearing.

You are invited to participate in a special session of creative thinking and fresh insight dedicated to inspiration.

We live in a world of constant change that requires us to be able to continually adapt and innovate in order to succeed. Unfortunately, many of us have forgotten how to delve into our raw creativity and leave behind the rigidity of the frameworks we have progressively interiorized.
This unique workshop seeks to reclaim our inspiration and imagination, rethink the unthinkable. It is ideal for people working in the creative arts as well as students, entrepreneurs, team managers, corporate leaders and anyone looking to implement their creative vision.

Inspiration is a vital driving force in our lives that moves us to create our best work and lights the way for new, authentic ideas. How do we invite, cultivate and harness inspiration so that we are able to bring these ideas into reality?
As a self-taught artist exploring various avenues of self-expression, Issa Sow draws a distinction between the phenomenon of inspiration itself and our task of making ourselves ready for it.
In the upcoming Inspiration Trap workshop, we will imagine ways we can invite and contain our inspiration, and well as keep our mind in the open, dynamic state as a receptacle or a “canvas” to collect, reflect and grow our ideas.
Feel free to bring along a personal object, a piece of clothing or even a small piece of furniture to play with during this hands-on experiment in innovative thinking. There are surprises and new elements in each session!

Issa =2
Issa Sow is a contemporary international autodidact artist known as Issa=2.
He believes in life being a journey of continual growth with each new

title: Queer Lit Club
location: Montclair Main - Tower Room
description:
This month we will be reading "Enigma Variations" by Andre Aciman.

"A passionate portrait of love's contradictory power, in five illuminating stories André Aciman, who has been called "the most exciting new fiction writer of the twenty-first century" (New York magazine), has written a novel that chronicles the life of Paul, whose loves remain as consuming and covetous throughout his life as they were in adolescence. Whether in southern Italy, where as a boy he has a crush on his parents' cabinetmaker; or on a snowbound campus in New England, where his enduring passion for a girl he'll meet again and again over the years is counterpointed by anonymous encounters with other men; or on a tennis court in Central Park; or on a sidewalk in early spring in New York, his attachments are ungraspable, transient, and forever underwritten by raw desire -- not for just one person's body but, inevitably, for someone else's as well. In charting the most inscrutable corners of desire, Aciman proves to be an unsparing reader of the human psyche, soul, and libido, and a master stylist of contemporary literature. With language at once lyrical, bare-knuckled, and unabashedly candid in Enigma Variations, he casts a sensuous, shimmering light over each facet of desire to probe how we ache, want, and waver, and ultimately how we sometimes falter and let go of the very ones who may want only to offer what we crave from them. Behind every step the hero takes, his hopes, denials, fears, and regrets are ready to lay their traps. Yet the dream of love casts its luminous halo. We may not know what we want. We may remain enigmas to ourselves and others. But sooner or later we discover who we've always known we were."

title: You Hear Songs, I See Them: Art, Music, and Synesthesia – An Experience with Sarah Kraning
location: Montclair Art Museum, 3 South Mountain Ave, Montclair, NJ, 07042, United States
description:
Step into an evening where music becomes color, movement, and art. Artist Sarah Kraning experiences sound through synesthesia, perceiving music as vivid colors, textures, and motion that she transforms into large-scale paintings. In conversation with Montclair Art Museum (MAM) Executive Director Todd Caissie, Kraning will discuss her experience with synesthesia and how it has shaped her artistic practice, exploring the connections between art, perception, creativity, and mental health awareness. The evening culminates in a live painting performance as Kraning transforms a Taylor Swift song into an original artwork in real time before the audience. The finished piece will be available through an online auction open to attendees through the weekend.

description:
WordPress Montclair Meetup
If you are running a WordPress site and are having issues and would like some help, then this Meetup is for you!

It's OK if you attend and only want to observe. We recognize this is how people learn. Given our time limit of two hours, we may not be able to solve everyone's issues, but we will try! If you are seeking help, please come prepared. Have your web site loaded in a browser, have your WordPress admin ready, along with a short list of issues you are trying to solve.

People helping are volunteers and may not be experts. There is risk to breaking your site! Please do not bring client or business sites that can impact reputations or revenue. If you have a staging site we can test things with, that is always preferred. If it is a production site, please create a site backup before having someone do any work on your site.

title: Girl Talk -Online Zoom Event -Dating Questions
description:
North Jersey Bowling, Volleyball, Tennis And More
This event is for females only, All ages are welcomed.

I asked Chat GPT some good Girl Talk questions and we will be taking turns answering them. We will go through as many questions as we can in the limited time.

Chat GPT says:

### Easy & Fun

* What’s your ideal weekend with someone you like?
* What’s your biggest dating green flag?
* What’s a small thing someone can do that instantly makes you like them?
* Are you more of a texter, caller, or FaceTime person?
* What’s your favorite kind of compliment to receive?
* What’s your love language?
* What fictional couple do you love?
* What’s your dream date idea?
* What’s something that always makes you laugh?
* Would you rather have a super romantic partner or a super funny one?

### Personality & Compatibility

* What qualities matter most to you in a relationship?
* What’s something you value in friendships *and* relationships?
* Do you believe opposites attract?
* What kind of personality are you usually drawn to?
* What’s something you’ve learned about yourself while being single?
* What’s one non-negotiable for you in dating?
* What helps you feel comfortable around new people?
* What makes someone memorable to you?
* Are you more introverted or extroverted when you like someone?
* What’s your communication style in relationships?

### Cute & Slightly Flirty

* What’s your biggest harmless crush right now?
* What’s the cutest thing someone could do for you?
* What kind of first impression usually catches your attention?
* What’s your favorite thing about getting to know someone new?
* What’s your ideal meet-cute?
* Do you fall fast or take your time?
* What’s your favorite thing about being single?
* What’s something sweet someone has done for you?
* What’s your type — personality-wise?
* What’s your idea of romance?

### Deeper but Still Comfortable

* What does a healthy relationship look like to you?
* What kind of support means the most to you?
* What’s something you appreciate more as you get older?
* What makes you feel genuinely understood?
* What’s something you hope for in your future relationship?
* What values are important to you in a partner?
* What’s something you admire in confident people?
* What kind of energy do you bring into relationships?
* What helps build trust for you?
* What’s one thing you think people misunderstand about dating today?

### Group Conversation Questions

* Who’s most likely to accidentally fall in love first?
* What’s everyone’s biggest green flag?
* What’s the best relationship advice you’ve heard?
* What’s a dating trend you don’t understand?
* What’s one thing people should normalize in dating?
* What’s your most wholesome crush story?
* What’s the nicest compliment you’ve ever gotten?
* What’s something attractive that has nothing to do with looks?
* What’s everyone’s dream vacation with a partner?
* What’s a movie relationship you think is actually healthy?

description:
A conversation about why money can feel like more work than it should, and where to start 
You’re doing well on paper. But your money still requires more attention than you expect it to. 
You’re keeping track, staying on top of things. It’s still not always clear how it all adds up by the end of the month. 
It’s a really common place to be, especially when your money is going in a lot of different directions. 
In this session, we’ll take a step back and look at why it can feel this way, even when you’re doing a lot right. 
We’ll talk about how to start seeing your money more clearly, what it looks like to be a little more intentional with your spending, and why certain expenses tend to throw things off. 
The goal is to make things feel a little more clear and give you a place to start.

Meet & Greet for Christian Singles, ages 25-45. This is an online event.

I asked Chat GPT some good questions to ask and we will be taking turns answering them. We will go through as many questions as we can in the limited time.

Chat GPT says:

### 🌿 Faith & Relationship with Values

* What role does your faith play in your daily life?
* What does a Christ-centered relationship mean to you?
* What qualities are most important to you in a partner?
* How do you usually grow spiritually?
* What’s something God has been teaching you recently?
* What kind of relationship do you hope to have one day?
* What are your biggest relationship values?
* What does healthy communication look like to you?
* What kind of family environment do you hope to build someday?
* What does commitment mean to you?

### 💛 Getting to Know Each Other

* What’s your favorite way to spend your weekends?
* What’s something people are usually surprised to learn about you?
* What’s a hobby or interest you wish you had more time for?
* What kind of personality are you naturally drawn to?
* Are you more introverted or extroverted?
* What’s your favorite worship song or Christian artist right now?
* What’s one thing that always makes you feel encouraged?
* What’s your favorite Bible verse and why?
* What kind of conversations do you enjoy most?
* What’s something you’re passionate about?

### 🤍 Deeper Christian Dating Questions

* How do you handle conflict or disagreements?
* What boundaries are important to you while dating?
* What does spiritual leadership look like to you?
* How important is church involvement to you?
* What are you praying for in your future relationship?
* How do you balance grace and accountability?
* What kind of support helps you feel cared for?
* What are some lessons you’ve learned from past relationships?
* How do you stay grounded during difficult seasons?
* What are your long-term goals and hopes?

### 💍 Bible Study Questions

* What’s one prayer God has answered in your life?
* What Bible story inspires you most?
* What’s something you appreciate in Christian friendships?
* What does “loving like Jesus” look like in relationships?
* What’s one quality you admire in strong Christian couples?
* What’s something young Christians struggle with in dating today?
* How can relationships help people grow spiritually?
* What’s one piece of dating advice you think is underrated?
* What’s your favorite way to serve others?
* What helps you stay encouraged in your faith?

### 🌸 Fun Questions

* Beach or mountains?
* Worship night or game night?
* Sunrise or sunset?
* Texting or FaceTime?
* Sweet snacks or salty snacks?
* Road trip or staycation?
* Big group hangout or one-on-one time?
* Fancy dinner or casual café?
* Books or podcasts?

### 📖 Fun but Meaningful

* Which person in the Bible do you relate to most and why?
* If you could ask God one question right now, what would it be?
* What does your “dream life” look like if God is at the center?

description:

title: Weekend Warrior Tennis (Saturdays)
description:
North Jersey Bowling, Volleyball, Tennis And More
We are typically beginner to intermediate levels playing in a friendly, sociable, and supportive environment while not being shy to a little friendly competition! We may rally freely in the beginning to warm up and then move on to some quick-rotation matches between 5-7 points. No formal teams here so everyone should be ready to both play with and against everyone else who shows up.

If you’re going to show up later than 8 AM then please tell us in the comments. Otherwise by signing up you agree to show up at 8 AM by default! Also, if you’re running late for any reason then please tell us in the comments – just make sure you’re not driving at the time and please always drive safely!

Also please be sure to bring your own racquet and water, as we don’t provide those! Also, I always have some balls for at least one court, but feel free to bring your own as well in case we need to branch out over more than one court!

Courts are subject to availability and weather. If you make serious plans to attend then please be prepared to cancel or adjust our location as needed. Furthermore, by attending you agree to be fully responsible for your own health and safety. Each person is responsible for their own decision to take a break, even if it has to be in the middle of a match! So health first, fun second, friendly competition third!

title: Creative Liturgy Workshop
description:
The prayers we recite by rote each week were not handed down fully formed from heaven—they were written by real people, reaching for words to express their hopes and fears, their loves and losses. Over time, those personal prayers became the shared liturgy of the Jewish people. But sometimes, the ancient words of others don’t quite resonate, which is why the process of prayer writing must be ongoing. Join Rabbi James Feder once a month to explore new liturgy being written for our current moment and take a hand at writing some yourself.

title: Let's Walk!! Brookdale Park
description:

If entering from Bellevue Avenue and park in the first parking lot on the left. We will be gathering near the the playground area.

if entering from Watchung Ave, park and walk up to the upper parking lot near the playground area.

title: The Joyful Art of Paper Folding NEW
location: Montclair Main - Auditorium, Montclair Public Library
description:
This is a free Adult School class. Click below to register.

In the Philippines, the young and the old love paper folding. They feel a sense of connection with their family and community by folding single sheets of paper to create beautiful objects, presenting them as thoughtful, handmade gifts for loved ones.

Paper folding is an enjoyable, creative, and meditative art form: transforming flat pieces of paper to three-dimensional objects. Through hands-on demonstrations and one-on-one instructions, students will learn and make simple to intricate structures, creating toys, flowers, birds, and utilitarian objects.

An accessible art, suitable for beginners and experienced folders, paper folding promotes mindfulness and relaxation. It improves fine and gross motor skills, spatial perception, and has other cognitive benefits.

title: Daytime Pool at Black Diamond Billiards
description:
North Jersey Bowling, Volleyball, Tennis And More
***Much like last time, trying something different. Unlike Clifton Billiards, this place has its own parking lot. They only do $20 day passes, but it's super laid back, we don't have to check in with management to change tables, and we can play as long as we want. This place also lets people bring their own food and drink, so if we want to order from a local spot, bring snacks or beverages, we are able. If this ends up being too far out for many people to join, I'll do the next one at Clifton Billiards or closer places going forward. Just wanted to see how this flew with the group.***

\*\*\* Expectations\*\*:
Pool cues are available at the location, expect mid to low lighting.
\*\* *What if I'm a beginner or only want to play with people at a similar level?*\*
Tables will be divided between beginners, intermediate players, and advanced. However, this depends on how many types of players come, so it will be divided as best as possibly available. If you would like game rules, please speak with Marc.\*\* Marc is also available to answer questions including how to hold the cue, stances, etc.\*\*

\*\*\* I feel like people aren't trying to be my friend.\*
\*Please remember that different people have different goals. Some may come to just play billiards, others may be there to meet new people or do something social, and some may be there to make long term friends. Find people that match your goals or be ok with others that may not.

description: Very (very) excited to present this quartet of contemporary heavyweights. Seed Artists founder PHEEROAN AKLAFF is one of the pre-eminent drummers in modern jazz. title: Schuylkill River Series: Pottstown-Royersford
description:
Metrotrails: NJ, PA, NY Metropolitan Area Hiking and More!
Join us for this point to point hike, the next in our Schuylkill series, between Pottsville and Royersford.
After meeting at Royersford, we will shuttle with as few vehicles as possible to the start.
We'll start by following a small creek greenway, then a bit of Schuylkill River Trail, but we must deviate from it because the 422 crossing is not yet open.
We'll use parallel roads on the opposite side of the river including another couple of parks and a cemetery to get to the next bit of the trail.
We'll continue along the trail, but deviate a couple of times to check out different side trails. We will be doing the Sanatoga Preserve as well as Independence Park Trail, then the Royersford Trestle to the end.
Distance will be about 15 miles. If needed, contact me at 908 343 8374.

title: 1776 in Western America: Forts, Furs and Frontier Online NEW
location: Montclair - Offsite, Montclair Public Library
description:
This is a paid Adult School class. Click here to register.

In 1776, while the 13 colonies were rising up against Britain, the rest of North America was occupied by a mixture of empires competing through an interconnected web of conquest, exploration, settlement and trade. From the Spanish missions in California to Native American trade centers on the Missouri River, Captain Cook’s voyage up the Pacific Coast in search of the Northwest Passage, Russian forays to Alaska for sea otter pelts, the Hudson Bay Company’s quest for fur-trade dominance, and the expanding Plains empire of the Comanche, we will explore how diverse peoples shaped a continent in flux. Maps, images and discussion will illuminate the year 1776 as both a revolutionary and continental turning point in the story of North America.

title: Marcel Duchamp: The Alchemist of the Avant Garde - Online NEW
location: Montclair Public Library
description:
This is a paid Adult School class. Click here to register.
Open the dictionary to the word “iconoclast,” and you will see a picture of Marcel Duchamp. He challenged the standards and beliefs of the art world and ushered in a new era of creative license—the reverberations of which are still felt in contemporary art today. Duchamp’s imagination was aroused by elements of Cubism, Surrealism, and even Pop Art, but his resourcefulness meant continuous self-reinvention and deliberate inconsistency. He once said, “I have forced myself to contradict myself in order to avoid conforming to my own taste.” Come and learn about his innovative works and the shockwaves they produced. A blockbuster Duchamp retrospective will be up at the Museum of Modern Art from April 12 to August 22.

description:
The Parent Academy is an engaging monthly program that runs September through June where parents and caregivers can learn practical tools and strategies to support their youth’s mental well-being. Each session focuses on a specific mental health topic and provides helpful resources and tips that can be used right away. 
These sessions are psychoeducational webinars, not to be used in place of clinical treatment. 
TOPICS: 
Suicide Prevention – Wednesday 9/17 12-1:00pm
Developed by the American Foundation for Suicide Prevention, the session is designed to help parents, teachers, and other caring adults recognize the warning signs of suicide in youth, initiate conversations around depression and suicidal thoughts, and guide them in helping young people access needed support and resources.  
Teen Dating Violence: Visible & Voiced – Tuesday 10/21 6:30-7:30pm
This session equips parents with the tools to recognize signs of dating violence in teens and respond with confidence. Learn how to spot red flags, support open communication, and help your teen build safe, healthy relationships.  
Less Stress, More Joy: Holiday Prep for Parents – Wednesday 11/12 12-1:00pm
This interactive webinar will help you plan for a more peaceful and meaningful holiday season. NJ4S will share simple strategies and practical tools to help you set healthy boundaries, manage stress, and prioritize your well-being.  
Spotting the Signs: A Guide to Youth Substance Use Awareness – Tuesday 12/9 12-1:00pm
PRESENTED BY Center for Prevention and Counseling
Participants will be equipped with tools and knowledge to recognize and respond to youth substance use.  
Suicide & Social Media – Wednesday 1/21 6:30-8:00pm
PRESENTED BY Jonathan Singer Ph.D., LCSW
This webinar will translate the most important research on social media and suicide risk into practical tips.  
Eating Disorders 101 – Tuesday 2/24 6:30-7:30pm
Information, signs to recognize, and resources will be shared on the topics of anorexia nervosa, bulimia nervosa, and binge-eating disorders.  
High Stakes: The Rising Risk of Youth Gambling – Tuesday 3/10 12-1:00pm
PRESENTED BY New Bridge Services Information will be shared about the growing issue of youth gambling, shedding light on trends, what to look for, and available resources.  
Parent/Caregiver Support for Children on the Spectrum – Tuesday 4/21 6:30-7:30pm 
The session will provide a safe, supportive, and empowering space for parents/caregivers of children on the autism spectrum to connect, share topics, and build resilience through tools for mental health, self-care, and caregiving.  
A Parent’s Guide to Youth Mental Health – Wednesday 5/13 6:30-7:30pm
This webinar will focus on the various aspects of mental health, how to have the conversation with a youth in your life, and what to expect after the conversation.  
Bored to Brave: Building Independence through Community Adventures this Summer – Tuesday 6/2 12-1:00pm
This webinar will cover the impact of changing schedules, empowering youth to reduce screen time, and creating opportunities within the home, neighborhood, and community. Our NJ4S summer programs will be noted, as well as free resources within the counties.

title: Weekly Labyrinth Walks, Wednesdays 11am-1pm
description: Weekly: Wednesdays 11am-1pm in the Sanctuary  Take your soul for a walk on the labyrinth.  We are pleased to offer labyrinth walks each Wednesday in the mid-day as a chance to connect with your soul in our beautiful sanctuary. The labyrinth is an ancient spiritual tool , a mode of “walking prayer” that invites us to go deeper in our walk with God.  Our labyrinth, modeled on one in Chartes Cathedral in France, sits as the center of our Sanctuary, a constant metaphor for our spiritual lives.  Just like the labyrinth, our lives are not linear, but filled with twists and turns.  Sometimes we make great progress, and other times we feel we are going backwards.  But if we trust in the path we will find ourselves in the center -- the heart of God. All are welcome to take their souls out for a healing walk... no experience necessary!  Check out this lovely write up on Baristanet from the Spring 2014. Watch this video to find out more about walking the labyrinth. If you’ve never done so come out one Wednesday evening and give it a try. It is a wonderful way to nourish your soul and spend some quiet time in prayer or meditation.

You are invited to participate in a special session of creative thinking and fresh insight dedicated to inspiration.

We live in a world of constant change that requires us to be able to continually adapt and innovate in order to succeed. Unfortunately, many of us have forgotten how to delve into our raw creativity and leave behind the rigidity of the frameworks we have progressively interiorized.
This unique workshop seeks to reclaim our inspiration and imagination, rethink the unthinkable. It is ideal for people working in the creative arts as well as students, entrepreneurs, team managers, corporate leaders and anyone looking to implement their creative vision.

Inspiration is a vital driving force in our lives that moves us to create our best work and lights the way for new, authentic ideas. How do we invite, cultivate and harness inspiration so that we are able to bring these ideas into reality?
As a self-taught artist exploring various avenues of self-expression, Issa Sow draws a distinction between the phenomenon of inspiration itself and our task of making ourselves ready for it.
In the upcoming Inspiration Trap workshop, we will imagine ways we can invite and contain our inspiration, and well as keep our mind in the open, dynamic state as a receptacle or a “canvas” to collect, reflect and grow our ideas.
Feel free to bring along a personal object, a piece of clothing or even a small piece of furniture to play with during this hands-on experiment in innovative thinking. There are surprises and new elements in each session!

description:
Step inside some of the most beautiful private gardens in and around Montclair—spaces you wouldn’t normally get to see. Each stop on the Roses to Rock Gardens Tour offers something different: lush rose gardens in full bloom, thoughtfully designed landscapes, hidden backyard retreats, and creative plantings that reflect the personalities of the people who care for them. Whether you’re a serious gardener, a design lover, or just someone who enjoys a beautiful afternoon outdoors, this tour is a chance to gather ideas, inspiration, and a fresh appreciation for what a garden can be. 
Start your day at Van Vleck House & Gardens, then explore at your own pace. We have 9 fabulous private gardens to visit! Also stop at Avis Campbell Gardens, which is lovingly tended by The Garden Club of Montclair and celebrating their 100th anniversary this year. title: Roses to Rock Gardens Guest Speaker: Evan Ralph
description:
Roses to Rock Gardens Guest Speaker: Evan Ralph, President of Back to Nature Home & Garden 
Saturday, June 6, 9:30 AM 
 
Have you seen these signs at aspirational gardens in the area? Learn from the award-winning landscape architect behind the firm, Evan Ralph. He will share his vision and process in his talk “From Desk to Dirt: How the Design, Build and Maintenance process come together to create exceptional gardens.” 
This $15 ticket is sold separately at the ticket link and includes a light continental breakfast. Start your day with fresh garden ideas and inspiration! 
 
About Evan Ralph: 
Evan is driven by a passion for outdoor living and a deep-rooted commitment to environmental stewardship. Over the past 11 years
at Back to Nature Home & Garden, he has grown from a Landscape Designer to President, guiding the company’s evolution with
creativity, hands-on leadership, and a relentless focus on quality.
An educator at heart, he’s always ready with a pair of pruners and a willingness to teach—demonstrating what true horticulture looks
like in action. Whether he’s leading a team or tending to his own garden, his motto remains the same: “Garden, every day.” 
Back to Nature Home & Garden  
A design/build landscape architecture firm serving New York, New Jersey, and Connecticut. 
What makes Back to Nature unique is all the different offerings that we have. We’re landscape architects, we’re landscape contractors and we’re also landscape maintenance. We see opportunities where others see challenges. We design and build customized outdoor spaces that are not only beautiful, but are ecologically friendly.

 About Bonnie Rapp**  
Bonnie had the honor of performing the lead role of Christine Daaé in the National Tour/San Francisco Company of Andrew Lloyd Webber's The Phantom of the Opera. Some of Bonnie’s favorite roles include Maria in The Sound of Music, Kate in Kiss Me, Kate, Cinderella in Rodgers and Hammerstein’s Cinderella, Louise in Gypsy and Sister Amnesia and Sister Leo in Nunsense, Nunsense II and Nunsense Jamboree. In addition, Bonnie has appeared in numerous galas, fundraisers, and Broadway concerts, including performances at Lincoln Center's Avery Fisher Hall.

title: Weekly Labyrinth Walks, Wednesdays 11am-1pm
description: Weekly: Wednesdays 11am-1pm in the Sanctuary  Take your soul for a walk on the labyrinth.  We are pleased to offer labyrinth walks each Wednesday in the mid-day as a chance to connect with your soul in our beautiful sanctuary. The labyrinth is an ancient spiritual tool , a mode of “walking prayer” that invites us to go deeper in our walk with God.  Our labyrinth, modeled on one in Chartes Cathedral in France, sits as the center of our Sanctuary, a constant metaphor for our spiritual lives.  Just like the labyrinth, our lives are not linear, but filled with twists and turns.  Sometimes we make great progress, and other times we feel we are going backwards.  But if we trust in the path we will find ourselves in the center -- the heart of God. All are welcome to take their souls out for a healing walk... no experience necessary!  Check out this lovely write up on Baristanet from the Spring 2014. Watch this video to find out more about walking the labyrinth. If you’ve never done so come out one Wednesday evening and give it a try. It is a wonderful way to nourish your soul and spend some quiet time in prayer or meditation.

title: NJ Code & Coffee - June meetup
description:
NJ Code & Coffee
Calling all New Jersey techies to the monthly **NJ Code and Coffee** tech community meetup at the EqualSpace ES550 Tech & Innovation campus!

Code and Coffee is an inclusive, informal networking/co-working session for those in tech (and the tech-curious).
That includes operators, founders, and investors. Developers, data engineers, UX/UI designers, data scientists, product managers, software engineers, solution architects... **all are welcome!**

People of all skill and experience levels can attend, we love it that way. Many people (optionally) bring projects to work on, and many other people (optionally) socialize the entire time. It's entirely up to you!

Come grab a cup of coffee and meet new people, share stories, find collaborators, talk about everything tech, talk about everything NOT tech, take a break from job applications, get away from the computer screen, make connections, make conversation, **make friends!**

**Agenda:**
**2pm:** Doors open, networking starts
**2:30pm:** Intro circle
**3pm:** networking continues
**5pm:** event ends

**The Intro Circle**
**Near the beginning of the event (about 2:30 pm), we will do a standup in a circle:**
We first talk about organizer announcements, updates, and logistics. Then we go around the circle where each person says:

\*your name and job title/ role in tech/ tech stack,

* What you can help others with,
\*What you would like help with,
* Job opportunities you're hiring for OR announce that you are looking for one. If none, that's cool.

After the introduction circle, everything is self-organized.

**Community Discord - come hang out before and after!:**
[www.codeandcoffee.chat](www.codeandcoffee.chat)

**The Venue**
Equal Space is a premium share-space created with multicultural business owners in mind, =SPACE equips founders with resources, programming and a powerful network.

Headquartered in the City of Newark, their share-space provides resources for startups, coaching for tech companies, and a wealth of intellectuals to collaborate and build with. The next wave in enterprises is being born within their walls. Become a part of the story: [EqualSpace.co/](https://equalspace.co/)

title: Weekly Labyrinth Walks, Wednesdays 11am-1pm
description: Weekly: Wednesdays 11am-1pm in the Sanctuary  Take your soul for a walk on the labyrinth.  We are pleased to offer labyrinth walks each Wednesday in the mid-day as a chance to connect with your soul in our beautiful sanctuary. The labyrinth is an ancient spiritual tool , a mode of “walking prayer” that invites us to go deeper in our walk with God.  Our labyrinth, modeled on one in Chartes Cathedral in France, sits as the center of our Sanctuary, a constant metaphor for our spiritual lives.  Just like the labyrinth, our lives are not linear, but filled with twists and turns.  Sometimes we make great progress, and other times we feel we are going backwards.  But if we trust in the path we will find ourselves in the center -- the heart of God. All are welcome to take their souls out for a healing walk... no experience necessary!  Check out this lovely write up on Baristanet from the Spring 2014. Watch this video to find out more about walking the labyrinth. If you’ve never done so come out one Wednesday evening and give it a try. It is a wonderful way to nourish your soul and spend some quiet time in prayer or meditation.

title: South Mountain Crest Trail
description:
Let's Walk!!
Let's Walk!! in South Mountain and visit Washington Rock and traverse a few of the many trails in the Reservation.

Washington Rock is Essex County Park System's bona fide Revolutionary War historic site, dating back to the late 1700's when Beacon Signal Station 9 was located here—one of 23 beacons built by General Washington to observe British troop movements quartered on Staten Island and New York City.

Seems like a great place to remember the nation's 250th birthday

This hike will be about 3-3.5 miles and mostly flat. The terrain is mostly dirt trails in the woods, so please wear sturdy hiking boots. **Bug spray and protective clothing is a good idea.**

Please arrive a few minutes early. We start promptly at the time posted. The hike should take us 60-90 minutes. **Please remember to bring water!**

Inclement weather may cancel this event. Please check the event page for comments prior to leaving for the meetup.

**Disclaimer:** If you join this event, please understand that you are responsible for your own preparedness and well-being and will hold no one else liable in case of injury or mishap.

title: Meeting at the Verona inn!
description:
Board Game Night At Verona Inn
We will be doing our first monthly meeting starting on **February 25th at the Verona Inn!** We will be meeting up to organize games starting at 7:30, with food and drinks available courtesy of our host! You can play any game provided by hosts or bring your own! If you do not have a friend group to play games, hosts will organize you into pods with other people who need players. There are **no dues**. Future meetings will be held on the **last Wednesday of each month.**

More information and ground rules:

* **The doors open at 6:30 but games do not start until 7:30.** I *highly recommend* coming in during this period to eat your food and drink ahead of time!
* **Please return the graciousness provided by our hosts and order at least one item! All venue specific rules apply to our club.** Future meetings depend on treating our hosts with respect.
* **All games must be returned to their owners when they announce that they are leaving.** If you are in a game in progress when the meeting ends but it is not borrowed you may continue playing!
* **Please place food and drink on a separate table or surface from your games** to help avoid stains and other damage.
* **Please engage with others in good faith, sportsmanship, respect and common sense.** *ABSOLUTELY NO harassment, getting physical, hurtful insulting, and persecutory language will be tolerated.* Repeat violators of venue rules AND/OR this rule may be asked to leave the event and not return.

title: Weekly Labyrinth Walks, Wednesdays 11am-1pm
description: Weekly: Wednesdays 11am-1pm in the Sanctuary  Take your soul for a walk on the labyrinth.  We are pleased to offer labyrinth walks each Wednesday in the mid-day as a chance to connect with your soul in our beautiful sanctuary. The labyrinth is an ancient spiritual tool , a mode of “walking prayer” that invites us to go deeper in our walk with God.  Our labyrinth, modeled on one in Chartes Cathedral in France, sits as the center of our Sanctuary, a constant metaphor for our spiritual lives.  Just like the labyrinth, our lives are not linear, but filled with twists and turns.  Sometimes we make great progress, and other times we feel we are going backwards.  But if we trust in the path we will find ourselves in the center -- the heart of God. All are welcome to take their souls out for a healing walk... no experience necessary!  Check out this lovely write up on Baristanet from the Spring 2014. Watch this video to find out more about walking the labyrinth. If you’ve never done so come out one Wednesday evening and give it a try. It is a wonderful way to nourish your soul and spend some quiet time in prayer or meditation.

title: Eagle Rock Reservation
description:
Let's Walk!!
JOIN US FOR A WALK. WE WALK AT A MODERATE PACE ON UNPAVED PATHS.

We will hike for about an hour - 3.5 miles. We will be walking on trails in the woods, so appropriate footwear, long pants & socks, and bug spray.

Will will meet at:
[https://goo.gl/maps/7rRRTiXCntdE1neD7](https://goo.gl/maps/7rRRTiXCntdE1neD7) Eagle Rock Trail Parking Lot by Kiosk#1

If you enter from Eagle Rock Way, go pass the Highlawn and stay left. There will be a parking lot at the end of the curve to your right.

Eagle Rock Reservation is 408 acres of hills, streams, and valleys located on the borders of West Orange, Verona, and Montclair, New Jersey. Though located in the middle of the most densely populated county in the most densely populated state in the country, the Reservation is mostly undeveloped and boasts an extensive trail system within its borders.

**Please make sure to RSVP and arrive 5 minutes prior to start time.**

FOLLOW US ON INSTAGRAM - letswalkmeetup

Disclaimer: If you join us for a hike, please understand that you are responsible for your own preparedness and well-being and will hold no one else liable in case of injury or mishap. Event will be canceled in the event of extreme weather.

title: 🥾 Let's Hike!! Jockey Hollow
description:
Let's Walk!!
Let's celebrate the nation's semiquincentennial (can you pronounce that?)

Come hike with us in the Morristown National Historic Park. We'll do about 3 miles along the Grand Parade loop, see a colonial era house and garden, and Revolutionary War soldier hut (replicas). It's a little like traveling back in time 250 years

[AllTrails: Grand Parade Loop](https://www.alltrails.com/trail/us/new-jersey/grand-parade-trail?u=i&sh=vgtzxk)

**PLEASE NOTE THIS WALK IS AT 09:30**
**Please arrive 5 minutes early so we can start on time.**

We've scouted these trails and find them appropriate for most of our members. If you've walked with us at Eagle Rock, this is similar in difficulty with just a little more up and down. There may be wet or muddy sections and a few rocks and tree roots. Please wear hiking boots/shoes and bring trekking poles or a walking stick, if you prefer.

Don't forget your water!

Inclement weather may cancel this event. Please check the event page for comments prior to leaving for the meetup.

**Disclaimer:** If you join this event, please understand that you are responsible for your own preparedness and well-being and will hold no one else liable in case of injury or mishap.

title: Eagle Rock Reservation
description:
Let's Walk!!
JOIN US FOR A WALK. WE WALK AT A MODERATE PACE ON UNPAVED PATHS.

We will hike for about an hour - 3.5 miles. We will be walking on trails in the woods, so appropriate footwear, long pants & socks, and bug spray.

Will will meet at:
[https://goo.gl/maps/7rRRTiXCntdE1neD7](https://goo.gl/maps/7rRRTiXCntdE1neD7) Eagle Rock Trail Parking Lot by Kiosk#1

If you enter from Eagle Rock Way, go pass the Highlawn and stay left. There will be a parking lot at the end of the curve to your right.

Eagle Rock Reservation is 408 acres of hills, streams, and valleys located on the borders of West Orange, Verona, and Montclair, New Jersey. Though located in the middle of the most densely populated county in the most densely populated state in the country, the Reservation is mostly undeveloped and boasts an extensive trail system within its borders.

**Please make sure to RSVP and arrive 5 minutes prior to start time.**

title: Help Desk - Bring Your Laptop, Yourself, and Your WordPress Problems
description:
WordPress Montclair Meetup
If you are running a WordPress site and are having issues and would like some help, then this Meetup is for you!

If you know some things, expert or not, and want to give back to the WordPress community, then this Meetup is for you too!

We will do our best to match a problem with a problem-solver. On-site and in real-time. Just bring yourself, your laptop, and your WordPress problems.

It's OK if you attend and only want to observe. We recognize this is how people learn. Given our time limit of two hours, we may not be able to solve everyone's issues, but we will try! If you are seeking help, please come prepared. Have your web site loaded in a browser, have your WordPress admin ready, along with a short list of issues you are trying to solve.

People helping are volunteers and may not be experts. There is risk to breaking your site! Please do not bring client or business sites that can impact reputations or revenue. If you have a staging site we can test things with, that is always preferred. If it is a production site, please create a site backup before having someone do any work on your site.

If you cannot find the group, please ask the front desk where the WordPress meetup group is meeting.

**PARKING**:
We've been asked to not park in the United Way lot behind the library as it could result in a parking ticket. Please find street parking or a parking deck.

\-\-\-
Join the **JerseyPress Slack** group to chat with others in our community and get help: [https://jerseypress.org/slack/](https://jerseypress.org/slack/)

title: Meeting at the Verona inn!
description:
Board Game Night At Verona Inn
We will be doing our first monthly meeting starting on **February 25th at the Verona Inn!** We will be meeting up to organize games starting at 7:30, with food and drinks available courtesy of our host! You can play any game provided by hosts or bring your own! If you do not have a friend group to play games, hosts will organize you into pods with other people who need players. There are **no dues**. Future meetings will be held on the **last Wednesday of each month.**

More information and ground rules:

* **The doors open at 6:30 but games do not start until 7:30.** I *highly recommend* coming in during this period to eat your food and drink ahead of time!
* **Please return the graciousness provided by our hosts and order at least one item! All venue specific rules apply to our club.** Future meetings depend on treating our hosts with respect.
* **All games must be returned to their owners when they announce that they are leaving.** If you are in a game in progress when the meeting ends but it is not borrowed you may continue playing!
* **Please place food and drink on a separate table or surface from your games** to help avoid stains and other damage.
* **Please engage with others in good faith, sportsmanship, respect and common sense.** *ABSOLUTELY NO harassment, getting physical, hurtful insulting, and persecutory language will be tolerated.* Repeat violators of venue rules AND/OR this rule may be asked to leave the event and not return.
source: Meetup: Board Game Night at Verona Inn

title: Council On Ministries- Multi Platform
location: UUCM-1-Mortenson (15) [Multiplatform]
description: The UUCM Council on Ministries (CoM) exists to report to UUCM, its Board and Co-Ministers on how our programs are accomplishing their particular mission while also furthering the broader mission of UUCM. Special attention is paid to any systemic or cultural obstacles hindering our ability to fulfill our mission as well as any conflicts. Its primary goals are to maintain UUCM's Mission & Vision, restore trust and relationship when frayed, and to keep all our interactions in line with UUCM's covenant. Best practices, connectivity, cross-pollination and successes are also reported. The CoM also provides assistance evaluating our ministries periodically at the discretion of the Board. Please welcome Council on Ministries liaisons into your meetings and planning when they request to observe your functioning; share with them also your minutes and other documents when requested. title: Meeting at the Verona inn!
description:
Board Game Night At Verona Inn
We will be doing our first monthly meeting starting on **February 25th at the Verona Inn!** We will be meeting up to organize games starting at 7:30, with food and drinks available courtesy of our host! You can play any game provided by hosts or bring your own! If you do not have a friend group to play games, hosts will organize you into pods with other people who need players. There are **no dues**. Future meetings will be held on the **last Wednesday of each month.**

More information and ground rules:

* **The doors open at 6:30 but games do not start until 7:30.** I *highly recommend* coming in during this period to eat your food and drink ahead of time!
* **Please return the graciousness provided by our hosts and order at least one item! All venue specific rules apply to our club.** Future meetings depend on treating our hosts with respect.
* **All games must be returned to their owners when they announce that they are leaving.** If you are in a game in progress when the meeting ends but it is not borrowed you may continue playing!
* **Please place food and drink on a separate table or surface from your games** to help avoid stains and other damage.
* **Please engage with others in good faith, sportsmanship, respect and common sense.** *ABSOLUTELY NO harassment, getting physical, hurtful insulting, and persecutory language will be tolerated.* Repeat violators of venue rules AND/OR this rule may be asked to leave the event and not return.
source: Meetup: Board Game Night at Verona Inn
